vt6_conclave.topic: How a pope is chosen: canon law, Universi Dominici Gregis and the May 2025 conclave that elected Leo XIV

claims.text: Canon 331: the Roman Pontiff is head of the college of bishops and holds 'supreme, full, immediate, and universal ordinary power'; canon 333 §3: 'No appeal or recourse is permitted against a sentence or decree of the Roman Pontiff.'

Canon 349: the cardinals form a special college that 'provides for the election of the Roman Pontiff' and assist him collectively or individually; canon 359: during a vacancy the college has only the power special law grants; canon 360: the Roman Curia acts 'in his name and by his authority'.

During a vacancy the College of Cardinals handles only ordinary or urgent business and preparation of the election; the Camerlengo (Cardinal Kevin Farrell in 2025) oversees temporal goods; heads of dicasteries cease except the Camerlengo, the Major Penitentiary and a few others.

Cardinals who have turned 80 by the day the vacancy begins cannot vote; Universi Dominici Gregis (1996) set a limit of 120 electors; voting is by secret ballot in the Sistine Chapel; a two-thirds majority is required, restored by Benedict XVI's 2007 motu proprio and confirmed in 2013.

Francis died 21 April 2025; the conclave opened 7 May 2025 with 133 of 135 eligible electors (Cañizares and Njue absent for health); threshold 89 votes; Robert Francis Prevost was elected on the fourth ballot on 8 May 2025 and took the name Leo XIV; Parolin presided as senior elector; inauguration 18 May 2025.

Leo XIV: born Chicago 14 September 1955; Augustinian (solemn vows 1981), Prior General; bishop of Chiclayo 2015; Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops from 30 January 2023; cardinal 30 September 2023; first Augustinian pope.
As of 9 May 2026 Leo XIV had held no consistory to create cardinals; 119 cardinals were of voting age; 29 would turn 80 within three years.
Leo XIV held consistories for discussion on 7-8 January 2026 and 31 May 2026 with no creation of new cardinals.

vt6_curia.topic: The Roman Curia under Praedicate Evangelium (2022): structure, economic bodies, office holders as of October 2026, how a decision moves

claims.text: Praedicate Evangelium was promulgated by Francis on 19 March 2022, entered into force on 5 June 2022 (Pentecost) and replaced John Paul II's Pastor bonus (28 June 1988, in force 1 March 1989).

The constitution lists 16 dicasteries (Evangelization; Doctrine of the Faith; Service of Charity; Eastern Churches; Divine Worship; Causes of Saints; Bishops; Clergy; Consecrated Life; Laity, Family and Life; Christian Unity; Interreligious Dialogue; Culture and Education; Integral Human Development; Legislative Texts; Communication) and economic bodies (Council for the Economy arts. 205-211; Secretariat for the Economy 212-218; APSA 219-221; Auditor General 222-224; Commission for Confidential Matters 225-226; Committee for Investments 227).
The Dicastery for Evangelization 'is presided over directly by the Roman Pontiff'.

Art. 44: 'The Secretariat of State, as the Papal Secretariat, provides close assistance to the Roman Pontiff'; Art. 45: three Sections (General Affairs; Relations with States and International Organizations; Diplomatic Personnel).

Principle 5 of the constitution: 'any member of the faithful can preside over a Dicastery or Office', acting by virtue of power received from the Roman Pontiff; Art. 17: prefects appointed for five-year terms; Art. 18: when the See is vacant 'all heads of curial institutions and members cease from their office' except the Major Penitentiary and the Almoner.

The Secretariat for the Economy 'functions as a Papal Secretariat for economic and financial matters', supervises curial institutions' administration and Peter's Pence, prepares the annual budget and the consolidated balance sheet, and must consult the Council for the Economy.

Secretariat for the Economy established 24 February 2014; prefects: George Pell 2014-2019, Juan Antonio Guerrero Alves SJ 2019-2022, Maximino Caballero Ledo from 1 December 2022 (no change listed in 2026).

Motu proprio 'Circa alcune competenze in materia economico-finanziaria' (26 Dec 2020, published 28 Dec, in force 1 Jan 2021) moved management of the Secretariat of State's investments, real estate and funds, including Peter's Pence administration, to APSA under Secretariat for the Economy oversight; announced in an August 2020 letter to Parolin.

Office holders listed as of 21 October 2026: Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin; Substitute Archbishop Paolo Rudelli; Secretary for Relations with States Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher; Evangelization: Leo XIV; Doctrine of the Faith: Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández; Bishops: Archbishop Filippo Iannone; Consecrated Life: Sr Simona Brambilla; Secretariat for the Economy: Maximino Caballero Ledo; Council for the Economy coordinator: Cardinal Reinhard Marx; APSA: Archbishop Giordano Piccinotti; Auditor General: Alessandro Cassinis Righini.
Parolin was still issuing documents as Secretary of State on 26 September 2026 (UNGA address) and 1 October 2026.

30 March 2026: Leo XIV named Archbishop Paolo Rudelli Substitute for General Affairs, replacing Archbishop Edgar Peña Parra, who became Nuncio to Italy; Archbishop Petar Rajič named Prefect of the Papal Household.

Leo XIV's first-year appointments included Filippo Iannone as Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops (September 2025) and Luis Marín de San Martín at the Dicastery for the Service of Charity (12 March 2026); Parolin and Fernández stayed; Leo told the Curia on 24 May 2025 'Popes pass, the Curia remains'.

Sr Raffaella Petrini was appointed President of the Governorate of Vatican City State on 15 February 2025, effective 1 March 2025, the first woman in the post, succeeding Cardinal Fernando Vérgez Alzaga; Leo XIV confirmed her on 9 May 2025.
The Fundamental Law of Vatican City State of 13 May 2023 confirms the pope's 'fullness of legislative, executive and judicial powers' and lets lay men and women sit on the Pontifical Commission.

Bishop appointments: bishops propose names; the nuncio investigates and sends a terna of three to the Dicastery for Bishops; the dicastery votes; the prefect presents the recommendation to the pope, usually at a Saturday audience; the pope decides; the process often takes six to eight months.
